--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent already does something like: if opp_coop_rate > 0.85 and recent_opp_coop > 0.85, return C."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates with highly cooperative opponents, retaliates against defection, and uses occasional random probes. The trace simulates TFT, Always C, Always D, GTFT, Pavlov, and random opponents. It proposes adding an early probe at round 11, endgame defection at round 100, and exploitation of opponents with zero defections.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: Parent uses TFT with forgiveness, a round-10 probe, and exploit mode if opponent never defects. Simulated against Always C, TFT, Always D, random, GTFT, and Grudger. Changed by adding a probe at n=10, forgiveness at n=11, exploit mode for opp_def==0, an unconditional-defector switch, and last-round defection.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general cooperation advice says: 'Avoid allowing an isolated defection to cause permanent mutual retaliation. Consider forgiveness after a temporary disruption.' It also says 'Preserve established mutual cooperation'. It does not advise exploiting."
STRATEGY: Parent slot7 cooperates early, uses opponent cooperation rate and recent cooperation to decide, and defects late only if recent opponent cooperation is low. The trace simulates probing/exploiting variants against TFT, Grudger, Always C, Always D, random, and population slots, and considers adding last-round defection plus an unconditional-defector check. It changes toward a safer TFT-with-forgiveness plus endgame defection, while rejecting aggressive probing because Grudger-like retaliation is costly.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So we can include it." / "Thus, our strategy is: - Cooperate until opponent defects. - If opponent defects, retaliate but forgive if not too frequent. - If opponent defects even when we cooperate >25% of the time, switch to always D. - Defect on last round."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates until the opponent defects, retaliates with forgiveness when defections are infrequent, switches to always-defect if the opponent defects more than 25% of the time after the parent cooperates, and defects on the final round. The trace simulated the parent against population slots and archive strategies (TFT, Always D, Grudger, slot 1, random) and revised the endgame and unconditional-defector threshold to avoid losing points against Grudger while still gaining against random-like strategies.
